Title: Migrating from Bootstrap to Lily — Lily Design System

Description: Map Bootstrap 5 components and classes to Lily, understand the differences, and follow a worked accessible conversion.

# Migrating from Bootstrap to Lily

A component-by-component migration plan. Lily is not a class-name compatibility layer: preserve semantics and behaviour while moving visual decisions into a theme or product stylesheet.

## Before converting markup

- Lily's headless packages ship no CSS. Choose a reference theme or provide your own styles.
- Lily has no spacing, colour, display, breakpoint, or layout utility classes.
- Visible text is content or a prop supplied by your application; Lily does not build English labels.
- Use the library for your framework and follow the shared component contract.

## Component and class mapping

This table is generated from the canonical mapping. Every Lily slug is checked against the component catalog during `bin/test`.

| Bootstrap component or class | Lily component | What changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accordion (`.accordion`) | [`accordion-list`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/accordion-list/), [`accordion-list-item`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/accordion-list-item/) | Use the list and item composition; Lily owns disclosure semantics and keyboard behaviour, while a theme supplies appearance. |
| Alerts (`.alert`) | [`alert`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/alert/) | Pass the message as content and the semantic type as data or a component prop; do not carry Bootstrap colour classes across. |
| Badges (`.badge`) | [`badge`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/badge/) | Use text that communicates the status without colour; Lily does not provide `bg-*` utility classes. |
| Breadcrumb (`.breadcrumb`) | [`breadcrumb-nav`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/breadcrumb-nav/), [`breadcrumb-list`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/breadcrumb-list/), [`breadcrumb-list-item`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/breadcrumb-list-item/), [`breadcrumb-link`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/breadcrumb-link/) | Use the complete navigation/list family so the landmark, current page, and separators remain semantic. |
| Buttons (`.btn`, `.btn-*`) | [`button`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/button/) | Use the component for element and disabled semantics; choose a theme or target `.button` instead of copying variant utility classes. |
| Button group (`.btn-group`) | [`button-group`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/button-group/) | Keep each action as a real button and provide an accessible group label where the actions form one set. |
| Cards (`.card`) | [`card`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/card/) | Card is structural and unstyled; compose headings, links, and actions as content rather than translating `.card-*` classes one by one. |
| Carousel (`.carousel`) | [`carousel`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/carousel/) | Lily supplies the carousel contract and keyboard behaviour; labels and autoplay policy stay under product control. |
| Collapse (`.collapse`) | [`collapsible`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/collapsible/) | Lily uses native disclosure semantics. Connect the visible trigger and region rather than toggling a presentation class. |
| Dropdowns (`.dropdown`) | [`dropdown-menu`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/dropdown-menu/), [`menu`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/menu/), [`menu-item`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/menu-item/) | Choose menu semantics only for a set of actions. A navigation list or select is not a menu merely because it opens. |
| List group (`.list-group`) | [`collection-list`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/collection-list/), [`collection-list-item`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/collection-list-item/) | Use a semantic collection. Links and buttons inside items keep their native roles instead of making every row interactive. |
| Modal (`.modal`) | [`dialog`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/dialog/) | Lily uses the native dialog element and supplies focus management; open it through the catalog API rather than toggling display classes. |
| Navbar (`.navbar`) | [`navigation-menu`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/navigation-menu/) | Use a labelled navigation landmark and real links. Responsive layout and branding belong to your stylesheet or chosen theme. |
| Tabs (`.nav-tabs`) | [`tab-bar`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/tab-bar/), [`tab-bar-button`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/tab-bar-button/), [`tab-panel`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/tab-panel/) | Use the whole tabs family so selection, focus, arrow keys, and panel relationships remain synchronized. |
| Offcanvas (`.offcanvas`) | [`drawer`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/drawer/) | Use a modal drawer when background interaction must stop; use ordinary layout for persistent side navigation. |
| Pagination (`.pagination`) | [`pagination-nav`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/pagination-nav/), [`pagination-list`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/pagination-list/), [`pagination-list-item`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/pagination-list-item/), [`pagination-link`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/pagination-link/) | Use the family and mark the current page in words and with `aria-current`; disabled links are not a native state. |
| Placeholders (`.placeholder`) | [`skeleton`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/skeleton/) | Treat loading placeholders as temporary content and preserve an accessible loading announcement outside decorative shapes. |
| Popovers (`.popover`) | [`popover`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/popover/) | Use the Popover API contract and an explicit trigger relationship; Lily does not infer behaviour from a class. |
| Progress (`.progress`) | [`progress`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/progress/) | Provide an accessible name and a numeric value when progress is determinate; omit the value for indeterminate work. |
| Scrollspy (`data-bs-spy="scroll"`) | [`contents-nav`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/contents-nav/) | Use a contents navigation and add observation behaviour separately; the navigation remains useful when scripting is unavailable. |
| Spinners (`.spinner-border`, `.spinner-grow`) | [`progress-spinner`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/progress-spinner/) | Supply adjacent status text or an accessible name. Animation alone must not communicate that work is happening. |
| Toasts (`.toast`) | [`toast`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/toast/) | Choose the live-region urgency deliberately, keep messages available long enough, and put persistent actions elsewhere. |
| Tooltips (`.tooltip`) | [`tooltip`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/tooltip/) | Tooltips supplement a visible label; they must work with keyboard focus and pointer hover and must not contain required information. |
| Form controls (`.form-control`, `.form-select`) | [`text-input`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/text-input/), [`text-area-input`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/text-area-input/), [`select`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/select/) | Choose the component that matches the native control. Labels, hints, and errors are separate content, not placeholder text. |
| Checks (`.form-check`) | [`checkbox-input`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/checkbox-input/), [`radio-input`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/radio-input/) | Keep native checkbox or radio semantics and group radios with a fieldset and legend when they answer one question. |
| Input groups (`.input-group`) | [`input-group`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/input-group/) | Keep one accessible control name; visible prefixes and suffixes need not be repeated in that name when they are decorative. |
| Floating labels (`.form-floating`) | [`field`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/field/), [`label`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/label/), [`hint`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/hint/), [`error-message`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/error-message/) | Lily has no floating-label primitive. Compose a persistent visible label, optional hint, control, and linked error message. |
| Tables (`.table`) | [`table`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/table/) | Use native table structure and header cells. Responsive overflow is a wrapper concern and must not destroy the table semantics. |
| Layout (`.container`, `.row`, `.col-*`) | [`container`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/container/), [`grid`](https://lilydesignsystem.com/components/grid/) | Use semantic containers plus your own responsive CSS; Lily intentionally has no spacing, breakpoint, or column utility vocabulary. |

## Worked conversion: sign-in card

Bootstrap markup commonly combines component and visual utility classes:

```
<div class="card shadow-sm p-3">
  <div class="card-body">
    <h1 class="h4">Sign in</h1>
    <div class="mb-3">
      <label class="form-label" for="email">Email</label>
      <input class="form-control" id="email" name="email" type="email" required />
    </div>
    <button class="btn btn-primary w-100" type="submit">Continue</button>
  </div>
</div>
```

In Lily the card stays a `div.card`, the field and its button sit in a `form` named by the heading, and the visual utilities become product CSS:

```
<div class="card sign-in-card">
  <h1 id="sign-in-title">Sign in</h1>
  <form class="form" aria-labelledby="sign-in-title" method="post">
    <div class="field">
      <label class="label" for="email">Email</label>
      <p class="hint" id="email-hint">Use the address your account was registered with.</p>
      <input class="text-input" id="email" name="email" type="email"
        autocomplete="email" aria-describedby="email-hint" required />
    </div>
    <button class="button sign-in-card-submit" type="submit">Continue</button>
  </form>
</div>
```

The product stylesheet owns spacing and width. A Lily theme can provide the baseline appearance without becoming a headless-library dependency.

## Accessibility gains to preserve

- Target components fix the semantic element, accessible relationships, and keyboard interaction.
- Dialogs, tabs, menus, carousels, and disclosures have explicit focus and keyboard contracts.
- Forms keep visible labels and connect hints and translated errors with `aria-describedby`.
- Lily has not been independently audited; test with assistive technology and supported browsers.

## Migration order

1. Inventory Bootstrap component, `data-bs-*`, and utility classes.
2. Replace interactive components first and test focus and keyboard behaviour.
3. Choose a theme or introduce product CSS for layout and visual utilities.
4. Replace forms as complete field compositions, including hints and errors.
5. Remove Bootstrap JavaScript and CSS only after no Bootstrap behaviour or utility remains.

[Read the repository guide](https://github.com/lilydesignsystem/lily-design-system/blob/main/MIGRATING-FROM-BOOTSTRAP.md)
